Se mantuvo el valor de primera persona plural y se incorporaron los cuatro patrones de concordancia informados. Se retiraron frecuencia nacional y equivalencias pragmáticas con Guatemala no demostradas por estos estudios.

Naro et al., resumen, líneas 475–479, describe las formas estándar preferidas y variantes frecuentes del habla popular. Zilles, resumen, líneas 64–66, delimita su análisis al sur de Brasil en 1970 y 1990. APA 7 y localizadores se añadieron a artículo y Evidence; assessEntry pasó con hash actual e índice local VERIFIED.
limitations: Los resultados de Zilles se refieren al sur de Brasil y a las décadas estudiadas; no se extrapolan a todo Brasil ni a Guatemala.

claims.summary: Naro et al. describe a gente and nós as first-person plural pronouns in Brazilian Portuguese; the cited standard pattern pairs nós with -mos and prefers third-person singular agreement with a gente.

locators.description: Cambridge article abstract, líneas 475–477: both forms denote first person plural; standard desinences and examples nós falamos / a gente fala.

claims.summary: Naro et al. report popular-speech variants nós fala and a gente falamos, so third-person singular is not presented as invariant across the speech data.

locators.description: Cambridge article abstract, línea 477: popular speech frequently uses nós fala and a gente falamos.

claims.summary: Zilles compares Southern Brazilian data from the 1970s and 1990s and describes the development of a gente as a pronoun increasingly replacing nós in speech in the studied region.

locators.description: Cambridge article abstract, líneas 64–66: grammaticalization, replacement of nós in speech, and comparison of Southern Brazil data from the 1970s and 1990s.

claims.summary: The four cited forms nós falamos, a gente fala, nós fala, and a gente falamos are explicitly mentioned by Naro et al.

locators.description: Cambridge article abstract, líneas 476–477; four forms and their agreement pattern.

sourceReferences.supports: Reference and agreement patterns with nós/a gente, including frequent popular speech variants.
